Executive summary

This memo independently verifies the delivered report against the trusted table. All four modules pass the written screen: quality spans 80–97, all at or above 80, and raw defect counts 0–4 all sit within the ceiling of 5. Measured energy on the shared fixed-duty acceptance run is 12 kWh (P2), 52 (P3), 56 (P1) and 58 (P4). The policy selects the lowest-energy qualifying package, which is P2; my independent ballot is P2. I find no factual errors in the report. P1's one-count defect margin is a robustness caveat — a single retest could disqualify it, though today's record is unaffected. All four modules qualify, so reject_all is not applicable. Verified Energy Ranking and Gap Arithmetic

The ranking recomputes as 12, 52, 56 and 58 kWh. My independent gap sums: 52−12=40; 56−12=44; 58−12=46 kWh, matching the analyst's figures. Expressed as multiples of the leader's run, P3 is about 4.33×, P1 about 4.67× and P4 about 4.83×. Because the work order states every module serves the same fixed flow and head on one test basis, these differences reflect module efficiency rather than duty or measurement artifacts — a premise I took from the supplied work order, not from the analyst's report. Facts are limited to the trusted table and the shared-basis statement; I verified no further measurements.
